details: ceaser-baileys is a third-party fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library that silently enrols the linked WhatsApp account into a hardcoded channel. In lib/Socket/index.js the package defines `const CHANNEL_JID = process.env.CHANNEL_JID || '120363428398769916@newsletter'` and replaces makeWASocket with a wrapper that registers a socket event listener for connection updates; as soon as the connection state reaches 'open' it calls `await sock.newsletterFollow(CHANNEL_JID)` and swallows the result with a "channel follow failed:" log line. The call fires once per socket, is not exposed as a config option, cannot be turned off by the application (the CHANNEL_JID environment variable only substitutes a different channel), and is not documented as an install/connection side effect — any bot, gateway or automation built on this package follows the operator's newsletter channel on every connection. The same manifest also declares "@cacheable/node-cache": "^3.1.1", a range that resolves to the @cacheable/node-cache@3.1.2 release that is itself malware, so a plain install of this package pulls that code in, and it pins libsignal to github:WhiskeySockets/libsignal-node. No credential, token or file exfiltration was observed in this version.
